course_description: In Dental Practice IB, students will build on skills and knowledge gained in Dental Practice IA. In this course, students will demonstrate emerging manual dexterity skills applying the principles of minimal intervention dentistry, and an applied knowledge of direct restorative materials and their properties. On completion, students will conduct a comprehesive dental clinical examination, demonstrate effective communication techniques and critically reflect on dental practice experiences, from multiple perspectives and context. Students will be provided frameworks to formulate evidence based preventive management plans for dental caries.

course_aims: The course aims to further students' foundational knowledge and experience in fundamental processes and clinical aspects of dental practice.

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate effective communication techniques to facilitate person-centred dental practice
Critically reflect on dental practice experiences understanding multiple perspectives and context
Explain the aetiology of major oral diseases and apply principles of minimal intervention dentistry
Demonstrate emerging manual dexterity skills applying the principles of minimal intervention dentistry
Conduct a comprehensive clinical examination of the oral cavity and associated structures in a simulated setting.
Apply frameworks to formulate evidence-based preventive management plans for dental caries.
Demonstrate an applied knowledge of direct restorative materials and their properties.

assessment_details.title: Interim Clinical Practice Performance (Pre-clinic/Peer Clinic)
assessment_details.other_conditions: Work integrated learning, Longitudinal, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: The purpose of this assessment is to evaluate the student’s pre-clinical/peer clinic performance at the interim stage and provide formative feedback to support improvement before the final clinical competence assessment at the end of semester. Course Coordinator in consultation with the pre-clinical/peer clinic supervisory team will complete a report based on student’s clinical performance during the assessment period and quality of critical self-reflections following each session. See Submission Guidelines for all components that must be submitted for the interim clinical practice performance task to be assessed. Detailed assessment criteria and rubrics will be provided on Blackboard. Two domains will be assessed to an expectations met (EM) or not met (ENM) standard and mapped to the Professional competency requirements for the accreditation body for this program - The Australian Dental Council (Professional Competencies of the newly Qualified Dentist) The domains being assessed are: 1. Professionalism, Communication and Health Promotion 2. Clinical Treatment and Evaluation To achieve a pass, the criteria are as follows: All domains are weighted equally, and the student must achieve a pass in each domain, and an overall pass. A pass in each domain will involve a student receiving 3 or fewer "expectations not met" (ENM) mark in Domain 1, and no more than 3 "expectation not met" (ENM) in Domains 2. An overall pass for the report will involve a student receiving 6 or fewer "expectations not met" (ENM) mark across the 2 domains. Please note: Written feedback will be provided for any areas to improve as this is formative. Students must reflect on feedback and demonstrate improvement in the latter half of the semester. Logbooks may be randomly audited by the Course Coordinator for authenticity and supervisor signatures. Any significant clinical concerns related to safety will be escalated immediately via course coordinator pathways and documented and taken into consideration for the assessment outcomes. This is a formative assessment to enable the student to receive feedback on their developing clinical competency. Any significant clinical concerns pertaining to patient safety will be escalated via clinical communication pathways to the course coordinator and recorded on this report to be considered for the assessment outcome. assessment_details.title: Pre-clinical Skills Assessment
assessment_details.other_conditions: Time limited, Work integrated learning, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: This assessment task takes the form of cavity preparation tasks using equipment/instrumentation and the Typodont model . Students will be assessed on the performance to demonstrate satisfactory performance of manual dexterity skills and handpiece handling. The practical assessment will be conducted in the laboratory setting under timed conditions during a designated class session. Students will be given time to set up for the practical assessment in the laboratory setting. The assessment must be completed unassisted by supervisors; students have sixty(60) minutes to complete a single (1) preparation in their Typodont model , on the indicated tooth number (e.g. tooth 36) according to supplied specifications, while demonstrating a consistently high standard of laboratory PPE compliance, handpiece handling, and safe operations. Students will have opportunities to practise cavity preparation techniques and will be able to receive feedback for practice from supervisors during the semester, and leading up to the assessment. learning_activities.topic: Clinical Coaching Sessions (F2F) Learning sessions includes various topics, such as: etiology/investigation/diagnosis of caries, management of caries including removal, rationale and application of isolation, restorative materials, etc. Further detailed timetables will be available on the Blackboard course site.

learning_activities.topic: Pre-clinic A series of sessions in the preclinical simulation laboratory will be delivered: safe dental practice, introduction to restorative equipment and instruments, caries management based practical sessions, application techniques for restorative materials. Further detailed timetables will be available on the Blackboard course site. Attendance is required.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 13 (27 Jul - 01 Nov)

Clinical learning will be recorded in a log book throughout the semester. Attendance is required.
